plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 mouse subcutaneous tumor samples (6 anti-PD-1, 6 isotype control), raw gene-level Salmon counts over 12000 genes, single batch, unpaired. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below median and must be inspected, not silently dropped. The research question is about immune/stromal cell composition and its difference between treated and control tumors — this is squarely an immune-deconvolution question, not a generic DE question, so the core analytical step routes to the immune-profiling-agent. Because this is mouse tissue, human deconvolution tools (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq, CIBERSORT) are inappropriate per the grounded flag from the knowledge service: their marker sets and reference profiles are human-derived and not specific in mouse tissue. mMCPcounter (the mouse-specific tool of record, confirmed present in the R GitHub track) is used instead. The plan proceeds: (1) sample-structure QC on the raw counts to characterize sample_01 and confirm no other outliers/batch structure before any downstream step touches the data; (2) convert raw counts to linear-scale TPM (gene length needed — obtained via the mouse Ensembl annotation package present in the environment) as mMCPcounter and other absolute-style methods require linear TPM/CPM, never log values; (3) run mMCPcounter to score 16 immune/stromal populations per sample; (4) statistically compare each cell-type score between anti-PD-1 and control with a two-group test (Wilcoxon/t-test per population with BH correction across the 16 populations, since these are per-sample scores, not gene-level counts); (5) as a complementary and more standard confirmatory analysis, run PanglaoDB mouse marker-based signature scoring (UCell) for the major immune/stromal lineages, explicitly labeled as a descriptive relative-enrichment score rather than an absolute deconvolution, to cross-check the mMCPcounter composition calls; (6) run the standard DESeq2 differential expression as context (per the grounded procedure) so that compositional differences can be reported beside, not instead of, the transcriptional contrast, and to let the report note which DE genes may reflect composition shifts (marker genes of a cell type found to differ); (7) a final report step integrates the QC findings, the deconvolution/scoring results, the group comparison, and the DE results with the caveats the knowledge service specified (sample_01 handling, mouse-vs-human tool caveat, scoring vs deconvolution distinction).
